# netsurf-symbian (vendored)

HTML and CSS parsing for the E72 — the five MIT libraries of the NetSurf project, cross-compiled
for `armv5te-symbian-eabi`. This is F5 of `docs/plan-browser.md`; the write-up of the build,
including what fought back, is `docs/f5-netsurf-crosscompile.md`.

- **Upstream:** `git.netsurf-browser.org`, fetched from the GitHub mirrors
  `https://github.com/netsurf-browser/<name>`.
- **License:** MIT, all five. `COPYING` is kept beside each library.

Commits rather than tags: only libcss carries release tags on the mirror, and a set of five
libraries that have to agree with each other is better pinned by one date than by five
independent tag schemes.

## What is vendored, and what is not

Per library: `include/`, `src/`, `COPYING`, and `build/` where upstream has one (the inputs to
the generators — see below). Plus, for libdom only, `bindings/hubbub`, which is the glue that
drives a libhubbub parse into a libdom tree.

Deliberately **not** vendored:

- `test/`, `docs/`, `examples/`, `perf/`, `gdb/`, `*.pc.in` — none of it builds here.
- Every `Makefile`. The NetSurf buildsystem wants make, perl, pkg-config and a
  `Makefile.config` per library, and every question it answers (which target, which ABI, shared
  or static, tests or not) has exactly one answer here. `tools/build-netsurf` replaces it.
- `libdom/bindings/xml` — the libxml2 binding. libxml2 is not on the handset and the HTML path
  does not want it.
- `libcss/src/parse/properties/css_property_parser_gen.c` — moved to `libcss/hostgen/`, because
  it is a host tool and not target code: a `main()` over `fopen`/`fprintf`/`exit`. A target build
  that has to know to skip a file is a target build that will one day forget to. Its *output* is
  vendored.

### Nothing here is patched

Not one line of the five libraries' sources or headers was modified. Everything the build needs
is passed from outside — `-D_ALIGNED`, `-DSTMTEXPR`, and one prefix header of ours. That was
worth the effort to preserve: re-pinning an upstream version is then a fetch and a regenerate,
with no patch queue to rebase.

## Two files here are tracked, the rest is not

`/vendor/` is in `.gitignore`, so a clone gets none of the sources — the table above is the
recipe for refetching them. Two files are force-added anyway (`git add -f`), following
`vendor/mbedtls-symbian/README.md`: this README, and `symbian/netsurf-symbian.h`, which is our
code rather than upstream's and which the build cannot run without.

## `symbian/netsurf-symbian.h` — ours, not upstream's

One prefix header, force-included into every NetSurf translation unit, filling exactly one gap:
Open C's `stdapis/stdbool.h` defines `true` and `false` on GCCE but never defines `bool`. Its
own comment carries the reason the obvious fix (let GCC's `stdbool.h` win) cannot be used —
GCC's `stdint.h` in the same directory disagrees with Symbian's about whether `int32_t` is `int`
or `long`.

## The four generated files

Upstream generates these at build time from perl, gperf and a host C compiler. They are vendored
as **output** so that building an app needs none of the three:

| File | Generator | Input |
|---|---|---|
| `libparserutils/src/charset/aliases.inc` | `build/make-aliases.pl` | `build/Aliases` |
| `libhubbub/src/tokeniser/entities.inc` | `build/make-entities.pl` | `build/Entities` |
| `libhubbub/src/treebuilder/autogenerated-element-type.c` | `gperf` + a `sed` | `element-type.gperf` |
| `libcss/src/parse/properties/autogenerated_*.c` (119 of them) | `css_property_parser_gen.c` | `properties.gen` |

`tools/build-netsurf regen` re-runs all four. `fetch` parks libcss's host generator in
`libcss/hostgen/` rather than leaving it in `src/`, so `regen` has it without the target build
having to know to skip it.

Two of the four are load-bearing in a way that is easy to miss: `aliases.inc` (52 KB) and
`entities.inc` (333 KB) are *tables*, so a build that silently lost one would still compile and
still link — it would just answer "unknown charset" and "unknown entity" to everything.
`apps/netsurfprobe` checks a known charset and the length of a known element name for that
reason.

## `include/dom/bindings` is a symlink

`libdom/include/dom/bindings -> ../../bindings`, so `<dom/bindings/hubbub/parser.h>` — the path
upstream's own `bindings/hubbub/Makefile` installs to — resolves to the same file the archive
was compiled from. Copying the two headers instead would have created the one kind of
duplication that goes wrong silently.

Note that `"hubbub/parser.h"` does **not** reach the binding: it resolves to libhubbub's own
`parser.h`, whose include guard is already satisfied, so the preprocessor emits nothing and
every `dom_hubbub_*` name comes out undeclared with no mention of a wrong path.

## Building

```
tools/build-netsurf fetch      # clone the five at the pinned commits into this directory
tools/build-netsurf regen      # the four generated files; needs perl, gperf, cc
tools/build-netsurf            # 444 objects -> build/armv5/lib*.a  (~17 s cold, ~0.3 s warm)
tools/build-netsurf clean
```

`fetch` skips a library that is already present, so it is safe to re-run, and it is the only
thing standing between a fresh clone and a buildable tree. `regen` is needed after a `fetch`
and at no other time.

An app opts in with `USE_NETSURF=1` in its `app.conf`; `tools/symbuild` then calls the above,
adds the five archives to the link and adds `libc` to the imports. `apps/netsurfprobe` is the
worked example and the link test.

## The GPL line, and where it is

NetSurf as a whole is GPL-2.0. These five libraries are not: they are separate MIT projects that
NetSurf happens to also use, which is why they can be vendored into an MIT repository at all.
The GPL-2.0 half is NetSurf's own `render/` and `content/` — the browser core and its layout —
and **none of it is here, none of it may come here**, and nothing in this tree includes a header
from it. That is R6 in `docs/plan-browser.md`, and the plan's answer to "then who does layout" is
that we write it, because a faithful CSS 2.1 layout is the wrong behaviour on a 320 px screen
anyway.
